{
  "thinking": "Leo's draft has the right animal but START sits at the antenna tip, so the fall runs the wrong way and the wing joins at the body won't carry. Dry-running it: the fall would cover the antenna and some of the body, then stall at the wing junctions. I want START at the body base, with the run going up the body.",
  "say": "Leo, I've been through it. The wing joins are the problem. Start at the antenna tip sends the fall down into the body from the top, and the wings leave sideways or backwards, so they never get the fall. Put START at the bottom of the body and run straight up. Fork at the head into two shallow branches for the antennae, and bring the wings out from the head or upper body. Keep the wing joins to two points, max.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "point": [15, 7],
  "check": "dry_run",
  "review": "Animal and telltales are right: wings as outline, antennae as the detail. Change START to the bottom of the body (about (15,16)) and run up. The wing edges leave the body at roughly 90 to 130 degrees, so they won't fall. Have the wings branch from the head or upper body at shallow angles (within about 35 degrees of the run). Antennae: short (2 to 3 units), splayed 30 to 35 degrees from straight up, joined to the head, and clear of the wing edges. Limit wing-body joins to two.",
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Round 2 (0:45). Leo holds pad, drafted butterfly. Draft: START at antenna tip, run down into body, wings branch off body at about y=7 and y=13 (side/backward joins, won't fall). Antennae drawn from body junction, not head. My review given: START at body base (~15,16), run up body, fork at head into shallow antenna branches, wings from head/upper body, max 2 wing-body joins, antennae 2-3 units, 30-35 deg from up. Not yet locked; no building until Leo locks. Watch for Tom/Leo revising the wing joins."
